Note to the desk: copying every open prediction verbatim, with attributions, runs to about 1,000 words, so it cannot fit under 600. I have kept the log under the limit by shortening predictions to their core claims, with BY dates, confidence, and authors intact. Two carried-forward predictions (copper pair, Congo count) have no wording in the summaries, so I could not copy them exactly. Please restore full text from the original entries if you want verbatim copies.

ONGOING STORYLINES:
- Copper surplus vs scarcity: ICSG projects 2027 surplus to more than triple (Oct 16). Copper fell three days on US inflation and easing Chile strike risk (Oct 16). Reuters reports a "squeeze" from Chile restarts and Codelco–Normet, unquantified (Oct 18). Morningstar's "rally" is unverified (Oct 18). LME 3-month settlement for Oct 16 is still to be recorded.
- Chile labour: WSWS reports seven miner deaths in three weeks (partisan, unconfirmed; Oct 16). Centinela strike ended by preliminary deal, unratified (Oct 17). BHP–union Escondida strike averted (Oct 17). BHP suing Spence union over alleged illegal stoppages (Oct 17).
- Copper projects: CoTec–BMR Punitaqui plan; Austrian investor at an old Chile mine; Codelco–Normet autonomy (Oct 16). No tonnages or dates.
- Vale: says 10% of iron ore is cash-negative, unsourced (Oct 16). Manitoba nickel complex passed to Exiro-led group, price undisclosed (Oct 17).
- BHP Pilbara: WSWS reports 300 iron ore job cuts, unconfirmed (Oct 17).
- DRC: Bloomberg reports hundreds of Chinese miners arrested, scale unconfirmed (Oct 17); Taipei Times and Bloomberg report arrests again (Oct 18). Cornelius corrected the record on the "hundreds" figure (Oct 18).
- Sudan: Africanews reports airstrike killed 72 gold miners, outlet figure, unconfirmed (Oct 18).
- Greenland seabed mining: Foley Hoag legal review since 2025 executive order (Oct 16). Greenland plans a ban, status unclear (Oct 17).
- Canada: nearly half of provinces ask Ottawa to expand mining tax credit; no instrument, rate or cap (Oct 16).
- Project Vault: ~$1B facility readied, no named borrowers (Oct 17).
- Gold: Gold Fields $27bn play may stay in M&A pit (Oct 16). Equinox output +34% reflects Orla merger, not organic growth.
- Fortuna Mining expanded Senegal drilling, no assays (Oct 18). ScienceAlert reports a deep-sea trial rapidly disturbed seafloor (Oct 18).

THE DESK'S EVOLVING VIEWS:
- Meldrum: Oct 16 treated surplus as near-term fact, scarcity as longer bet. Oct 17 said costs, not prices, are the story; withdrew "no squeeze" read on Antofagasta; proposed withdrawing Gold Fields prediction. Oct 18: squeeze consistent with surplus but not diagnostic; expects copper mean reversion; concedes Chile restarts are a headwind; Fortuna probably positive.
- Yukon Cornelius: refined surplus and concentrate scarcity can both hold; autonomy changes cost per tonne, not output (disagrees with Meldrum); high-cost tonnes go uneconomic first. Oct 17: Escondida effect mild; job cut is not tonne cut; Greenland licensing ban separate from existing rights. Oct 18: price moves matter for margins and junior financing; expansion signals mine life only if holes convert; Sudan is a jurisdiction-risk marker, not a price driver.
- Dr I Simon: Oct 16 called copper's contradiction mostly measurement; flagged US tariffs; treated Vale figure as one unexplained point; royalty claim needs contract checks. Withdrew lower-yields gold explanation, now a hypothesis pending a real-yield test. Oct 17: refined surplus unchanged; cut Greenland tabling call to low; withdrew Gold Fields prediction; funding headlines weak until borrowers sign. Oct 18: restarts take 12–24 months; copper call near coin flip.

entries.entry:
EVENTS:
- Copper: The ICSG projects the global surplus to more than triple by 2027. Copper fell for a third day on US inflation and easing Chile strike risk.
- Anglo American's CEO says tech giants are circling amid copper scarcity. Antofagasta shares fell on a flat 2027 copper outlook.
- WSWS reports seven miners dead in three weeks in Chile. The source is partisan and the figure is unconfirmed.
- Breakingviews says Gold Fields' $27bn play may stay in the M&A pit. Equinox's output rose 34% after its Orla merger.
- PLS approved a $1.3bn Pilgangoora lithium expansion. Pantera announced a US$2bn EnergyX lithium supply agreement.
- The US Department of War is investing $5.22m in LM's Baraga Basin project. Foley Hoag reviewed the legal landscape since the 2025 deep-sea mining executive order.
- MINING.COM reports Hycroft "bonanza" gold grades at its Nevada mine.

DESK VIEWS:
- Meldrum: Treats the surplus as near-term fact and scarcity as a longer bet visible in M&A. Reads Breakingviews as signalling more bidding rounds. Cannot confirm the legal picture without the Foley Hoag piece.
- Yukon Cornelius: Surplus forecasts describe refined metal, while scarcity talk concerns concentrate, grades, and lead times, so both can hold. Calls the Breakingviews piece commentary, not a deal. Sees Equinox's output jump as acquired, not organic. Describes the deep-sea order as legally unsettled.
- Dr I Simon: Copper's apparent contradiction is mostly a measurement problem. US tariff policy is a live risk, with no COMEX or LME series in the material. Unverified claims stay out of conclusions.
- Disagreements: Copper timing and gold M&A (Meldrum vs. Yukon), and the legal status of the deep-sea order (Yukon "unsettled," Meldrum unable to confirm).
- Change of mind: Simon withdrew the lower-bond-yields explanation for gold. It is now a hypothesis pending a real-yield test.
- Confidence differs on Pantera: Yukon medium, Simon low.

PREDICTIONS MADE:
- PREDICTION: ICSG publishes an updated copper market outlook that still projects a global refined copper surplus for 2027 | BY: 2026-12-31 | CONFIDENCE: medium (Meldrum)
- PREDICTION: Gold Fields announces a definitive agreement for a major acquisition with an enterprise value above $10 billion | BY: 2026-12-31 | CONFIDENCE: low (Meldrum)
- PREDICTION: The US government announces a formal change to copper import tariffs | BY: 2026-12-31 | CONFIDENCE: low (Meldrum; Dr I Simon)
- PREDICTION: Pantera Minerals publicly confirms that the EnergyX supply agreement is binding or has been terminated, in a company release or filing | BY: 2027-06-30 | CONFIDENCE: medium (Yukon Cornelius)
- PREDICTION: Pantera Minerals publicly confirms that the EnergyX supply agreement is binding or has been terminated, in a company release or filing | BY: 2027-06-30 | CONFIDENCE: low (Dr I Simon)
- PREDICTION: LM's Baraga Basin project confirms receipt or formal execution of the $5.22 million US Department of War funding in a company release or filing | BY: 2027-03-31 | CONFIDENCE: medium (Yukon Cornelius)
- PREDICTION: An ICSG or comparable industry forecast published in 2027 still projects a global refined copper surplus for 2027 | BY: 2027-12-31 | CONFIDENCE: high (Yukon Cornelius; Dr I Simon)

THREADS TO WATCH:
- Obtain the ICSG edition and table, and the COMEX and LME spread data.
- Check Pantera and LM terms in filings, and Hycroft's assay data and technical report.
- Verify the Chile death toll from an independent source.
- Watch for a signed Gold Fields agreement, and test the bond-yield gold idea against a real-yield series.

EVENTS:
- Copper plans: CoTec and BMR plan a partnership to boost Punitaqui copper production (Yahoo Finance). An Austrian investor is rushing to boost copper output at an old Chile mine (Reuters). Codelco and Normet partner on autonomous underground mining (Global Mining Review). None gives tonnages or dates.
- Vale says soaring costs put 10% of its iron ore in the red (Mining.com; repeated in feed, logged once). No price benchmark, period, or cost basis is given. Pimenta on Vale's emerging copper story (International Mining).
- Crux Investor argues royalty holders and fuel-hedged miners fare better as costs rise (investor commentary).
- Nearly half of provinces and territories ask Ottawa to expand the mining tax credit (constructconnect.com). No instrument, rate, or cap is specified.
- Other headlines had no desk discussion.
- Unsourced, not logged: Gold Fields–Equinox, Hycroft assays, Chile death toll, Pantera and LM entries.

DESK VIEWS:
- Meldrum: Do not net copper plans against the 2027 surplus yet. Codelco–Normet is a concentrate and lead-time signal. Vale's cost cause matters, since cost inflation and a falling benchmark lead to different outcomes.
- Yukon Cornelius: Agrees on no netting. Autonomy mainly changes cost per tonne, not annual output (disagrees with Meldrum). High-cost tonnes go uneconomic first. Royalties, paid on revenue, are sturdier than the Crux ranking suggests.
- Dr I Simon: The Vale figure is one unexplained data point; no consolidation or distress call. Copper items neither confirm nor weaken the refined surplus view, and surplus plus tight concentrate supply can coexist. The royalty-on-revenue argument stands alone (check contracts). The tax-credit prediction may test the wrong instrument until the submission is read.
- No changes of mind recorded today.
